what: RAISED BY THE MANAGER 2026-09-22T12:50Z as an addendum to the E20 dispatch, in its own words: 'only `failed` can push an event, while `blocked`, `review_ready` and `completed` are SILENT BY DESIGN. That is WHY four lanes sat dead for over an hour today... the manager's only view of lane state is a PULL it must choose to make, so "the manager did not notice" was structurally guaranteed, not a lapse of attention.' It asked whether push-on-stop plus a 2-hourly sweep is sufficient. ANSWERED WITH A MEASUREMENT RATHER THAN AN OPINION, and the answer is NO. POPULATION: the 60 most recent sessions on this account, list_sessions(mine=true) read 2026-09-22T13:02Z. BY status_bucket: COMPLETED 43, WORKING 7, REVIEW_READY 4, BLOCKED 4, FAILED 2. [!] THE PUSH WIRE REACHES FAILED ONLY, SO IT COVERS 2 OF 60 SESSIONS. The conditions that actually cost money are BLOCKED (4 sessions, $1,347.60) and finished-but-unarchived (22 sessions, $2,088.73) = 26 conditions, and the wire covers ZERO of them. The $1,343.06 lane that has sat 72.8 hours having never committed a line is BLOCKED -- squarely in the silent set -- which is why it lasted three days rather than an hour. [!] AND THE REPLY WIRE HAS THE SAME HOLE ONE LEVEL DOWN, which is the sharper half: the lane->manager channel is a create_trigger the LANE must choose to fire. A lane that dies mid-turn, exhausts its budget, or hits a permission wall cannot fire it -- so the wire structurally cannot cover the cases it exists for, because A BLOCKED LANE CANNOT REPORT THAT IT IS BLOCKED. It helps for lanes that finish cleanly and not at all for the ones that do not. [!] AND THE 2-HOURLY SWEEP FIRES INTO THE MANAGER'S OWN SESSION, so it is a reminder a manager can skip -- reason (5) from the operating plan, the one that killed DUE.md. The manager said as much itself when dispatching E20. [!] WHAT E20 BUILT AND WHY IT IS NOT THE ANSWER YET: a Routine firing a FRESH session (so the manager is not in the path) was created, fired, and DISABLED, because the fired session has no repo checkout and no MCP connectors -- see PI-20260922-THE-LANE-WATCHDOG-ROUTINE-FIRES-SESSIONS-WITH-NO-REPO-AND-NO-MCP-SO-IT-IS-DISABLED-AND-THE-INVARIANT-IS-STILL-VOLUNTARY. So BOTH candidate mechanisms are currently unavailable and the detection is a pull. [!] THIS IS FILED RATHER THAN ONLY REPORTED BECAUSE A MESSAGE IS NOT A DISPOSITION. The judgement was delivered to the manager as a report-back trigger at 13:28Z; a trigger prompt is a chat message with extra steps, and close-out check 4 is explicit that neither is filing. The decision owed is whether lane-stop detection becomes a push (a platform capability nobody here controls) or stays a pull with a named non-optional mechanism.
